newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Tuesday after the exchange tightened control over the repo business, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 13.01 percent from 15.00 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market plunged to 2.1 million lots from 4.7 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said the Shanghai stock exchange recently tightened supervision over the repo market, in particular checking whether brokerages were using the same spot state debt positions as warrants for more than one repo transaction.
Controls were tightened after Beijing recently took a series of measures to cool down securities trading, they said.

"Institutions including securities houses built much fewer positions on Tuesday due to the tightened control," a trader said. "Even a new (domestic) A share issue on the exchange today could not support the repo rates."
Traders said they expected the repo rates to move around the current level on Wednesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday led by the market leader 10-year bond that matures in June 2000, traders said.
The 10-year bond was the most actively traded, rising to 121.33 yuan from 121.20 yuan. Total volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.1 million lots from 1.2 million lots.
Traders said the high yields of existing contracts at more than 10 percent on average supported Tuesday's rise, adding the contracts still had potential to rise in the short term.
